gamefaqs.product: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998)

format: DexDrive .n64: "123-456-STD" and a 0x1040-byte header (DexPlorer comments), then a 32 KiB Controller Pak with one GameShark cart-save note "ZLZL" (3BADD1E5/FADE), 24 pages: a 4-byte little-endian length 0x8000, then the cartridge's 32 KiB SRAM compressed with LZARI (6054 bytes); it decodes to the SRAM in console byte order

verified.converted_with: tools/gamefaqs/n64-dexdrive.py convert the-legend-of-zelda-ocarina-of-time-1998.1263.n64 OUT: dexdrive: pak = the 32768 bytes after the 0x1040-byte header; ID block checksums 0101/FEFD wrong in every copy, rewritten as 0101/FEF1; cart-save note 'ZLZL' (GameShark 3BADD1E5/FADE): LZARI, 6054 bytes -> 32768

converted_standalone.how: the same bytes as the .srm regions, as standalone Mupen64Plus keeps them: <GoodName (32 chars)>-<MD5 8>.eep/.sra/.fla/.mpk in its save folder

note: Ocarina of Time saves to cartridge SRAM, not to a Controller Pak: this is a GameShark Memory Card Manager backup of the SRAM onto the pak, which the device compresses with LZARI behind a 4-byte little-endian length. No public tool decodes it (save-file-converter handles only uncompressed EEPROM notes); the converter's LZARI decoder (Okumura's LZARI.C) gives a 32 KiB SRAM whose three files carry valid checksums. The cartridge revision is not recorded; Rev 2, the library's release, was used. Byte-identical to GameFAQs 1260.
